findings.title: A template can arm 20 every-minute autonomous schedules that one autonomy toggle enables at once
findings.description: Creation now materializes a template's declared schedules. MAX_DECLARED_SCHEDULES is 20 and the reader accepts '* * * * *'. Independently, set_autonomy_status_logic force-enables every schedule on an agent when autonomy is turned on, with no filter.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) A public github: template declares 20 entries with cron '* * * * *' and enabled: true. 2) A creator (or an agent-scoped MCP key holding create_agent) creates an agent from it; all 20 rows are written. 3) Nothing fires: agent_ownership.autonomy_enabled defaults to 0 and the scheduler gates on it (src/scheduler/service.py:844). 4) The operator later enables autonomy for an unrelated reason; set_autonomy_status force-enables all 20 at once -> ~28,800 LLM turns/day on the operator's key.
findings.impact: Cost amplification on the operator's own API key or subscription, reachable with one template choice plus one unrelated toggle.
mitigations_present: agent_ownership.autonomy_enabled defaults to 0; scheduler gates on it (this is the control that holds)
ghost agents skipped; ent#69 refuses ephemeral callers
findings.severity_rationale: MEDIUM not HIGH: the amplification capability is pre-existing (no per-agent schedule cap has ever existed, so 20 deliberate API calls always achieved the same). #89 reduces friction, it does not create the capability.
findings.recommendation: Make set_autonomy_status stop clobbering per-schedule 'enabled' intent. No change required in this PR.
